svg.title: Fabric Implementation Delivery Chain — Environments to Operational Readiness
svg.desc: A five-phase delivery lifecycle diagram showing workspace staging, deployment pipeline promotion with variable libraries, testing with mirroring replication triggers, security trade-offs, and operational readiness with item recovery.
svg.text: Fabric Implementation Delivery Chain: Environments to Readiness
Staged Workspaces ➔ CI/CD Pipelines & Variable Libraries ➔ Testing Gates ➔ Security Posture ➔ Item Recovery

g.title: Workspace environments (Dev / Test / Production) — Three workspaces — Dev, Test, and Production — form the promotion chain that deployment pipelines move items across.
g.text: Dedicated three-tier workspace isolation backing the release lifecycle
• Each stage represents a dedicated Fabric workspace with isolated capacity mapping
• Production workspace write access strictly restricted to Deployment Pipeline service principal
• Map Dev and Test to shared trial/pay-as-you-go capacity units to optimize cost.
• Production maps to dedicated F-SKU capacity, isolating executive reports from dev load.
• Git integration enables branch-per-developer workflows synchronizing with remote repo.
Standard: Never author or edit items directly inside Production workspaces!

g.title: Deployment Pipelines — promote + Variable Libraries — Deployment Pipelines promotes items across Dev, Test, and Production while Variable Libraries swap in environment-specific connection strings, gated by a pull request.
g.text: Phase 2: CI/CD Deployment Pipelines & Variable Libraries
Automated promotion engine with parameter overrides & PR approval gates
• Selective item deployment: Compare stages and deploy only changed artifacts
• Variable Libraries automatically swap target endpoints, lakehouses, and SQL server URLs
• Schema comparison tools highlight additions, modifications, and deletions between stages.
• Enforce branch protection policies: PR approval required before Git merge & promotion.
• Deployment history provides full audit trails of who promoted what item and when.
Eliminates manual config drift and post-deployment manual tampering.

g.aria-label: Testing — quality gates + mirroring replication trigger
g.title: Testing — quality gates + mirroring replication trigger — Promoted items are validated for quality before serving, and any mirrored database item needs its replication triggered manually since promotion alone leaves it empty.
g.text: Phase 3: Testing Quality Gates & Mirroring Replication
Data validation suite & manual replication trigger for promoted mirrored items
• Automated unit & regression tests validate Lakehouse, Warehouse & Direct Lake models
• When Deployment Pipelines promotes a Mirrored Database, replication does NOT start automatically.
• Target workspace receives a configured but EMPTY item until an operator triggers replication.
• Starting replication executes a complete initial load from source before streaming CDC begins.
Trap: Running tests against a newly promoted mirror without triggering replication
evaluates against 0 rows, masking broken downstream joins and false positive passes!

g.title: Security — workspace & tenant access controls — Workspace-level Block Public Access and tenant-level private links are real architectural trade-offs: both disable Deployment Pipelines and Fabric SQL Database outright, not just restrict them.
g.text: Phase 4: Security Access Controls & Network Trade-Offs
Tenant & workspace boundary policies governing data isolation
• Deployment Pipelines are DISABLED when Block Public Access is active on the workspace.
• Fabric SQL Database is UNSUPPORTED under workspace public-access blocking.
• On-premises data gateways stop registering under tenant-wide private link isolation.
• Power BI Publish to Web, email subscriptions, PDF export, and Copilot are disabled.
Design Rule: Security policies must be evaluated as architectural trade-offs, not enabled blindly.
If Deployment Pipelines are required, public access blocking cannot be applied to target workspaces.

g.aria-label: Operational readiness — Item Recovery + monitoring gate
g.title: Operational readiness — Item Recovery + monitoring gate — Release is accepted only once monitoring evidence exists and the Item Recovery retention window is confirmed as the safety net for the newly promoted items.
g.text: Phase 5: Operational Readiness, Item Recovery (Up to 90 Days) & Sign-Off
Final operational acceptance gate before production workloads are opened to business consumers
• Recycle Bin safety net for accidental drops
• Fabric Activator alerts on job failures
• Signed off by platform architect & owner
• Failure Action: Rejects release back to Dev
If operational readiness validation fails (e.g. unmonitored failures, capacity exhaustion, or broken recovery policies),
the release is rejected and routed back to Phase 1 (Dev) via Git branch iterations before re-entering Deployment Pipelines.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Delivery & Architecture Specs.
